title.narrative: Restore and improve food production and agricultural livelihoods of El Niño-impacted households through cash and voucher assistance and climate smart agriculture in Dowa, Chikwawa and Nsanje districts

description.narrative: Through this project, FAO Malawi will implement emergency cash-based response interventions to support 5,850 vulnerable households affected by the 2023/24 El Nino in Chikwawa and Nsanje districts by promoting more sustainable agricultural and food production during the main agricultural and winter seasons 2024/25. 3,8500 households will receive unconditional cash transfers for a duration of six months during the main agricultural and winter season 2024/25, with a monthly transfer value of MWK 70,000 (USD 40) per household to address their basic needs, thus sustaining and promoting agriculture and food production and preventing negative coping strategies. The cash distribution will occur in two instalments and will be combined with capacity building and awareness activities on the effective use of the cash received for addressing basic food needs, Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA), and child and women protection. Also, a cash for work intervention, targeting 2,000 beneficiary households will be implemented to support the rehabilitation of community productive assets and restore agricultural activities through reforestation and land rehabilitation. Each household involved in cash for work activities will receive MWK 48,000/month (USD 27.5) to work for two months. FAO Malawi will engage a local Implementing Partner to support the implementation of activities under this component and to ensure the localization of the intervention.Under the CLIMATE ENVELOPE, in Dowa district FAO Malawi will work to improve Dzaleka refugee and host community farmers’ capacity and knowledge on high value crops production and environmental management by facilitating access to quality agricultural inputs through electronic vouchers. It will also support the adoption of CSA practices, while strengthening the beneficiaries' capacities to resume and continue their agriculture livelihood activities. This intervention is expected to protect beneficiaries’ livelihoods affected by El Nino and reduce the period in which families require external assistance support, including food assistance. Additionally, the combination of the agricultural input distribution with trainings on CSA through the Lead Farmer (LF) approach will allow beneficiaries to ensure the efficient use of the assistance package, and enhance their capacity to adapt to climate extreme events in a timely manner thanks to the possibility of passing on knowledge within the community, including that will remain beyond the project duration. This approach will also promote the reduction of pressure on the natural environment and ecosystem surrounding the refugee camp and at the same time allow to better control the rampant deforestation that is occurring in the area in order to access energy sources (i.e. firewood and charcoal) as well as to continue farming and livelihood activities. This component will target 930 households (i.e. 4,464 people) living inside and outside Dzaleka refugee camp (60% of beneficiary refugee households and 40% of host communities beneficiary households) with emergency distribution of agricultural inputs through electronic vouchers and training on the adoption of CSA and post-harvest management techniques using the LF approach. This component will further promote the protection and restoration of the natural ecosystems in Dzaleka camp and the surrounding host community through capacity building activities and the promotion of natural resources regeneration in existing forests to increase community resilience to future climate shocks. FAO will also facilitate community-led Gender Transformative and Household Approaches for promotion of gender equality and inclusion in climate adaptation actions.FAO Malawi will deploy IT solutions such as the Identification, Delivery and Empowerment Application (IDEA) platform to facilitate beneficiary registration and tracking, and support the delivery and tracking of assistance through this modality.
